added.text: Distinguish null containers, empty containers, and null elements according to the contract. Never substitute NullSafe empty-container normalization for a required non-null input check. When at least one element is required, enforce non-emptiness separately; Require.noNulls and NullSafe.copyTo* element checks alone do not establish it.

Production and test code must not retain unused type imports or static imports. Check and remove unused imports after creating, changing, or refactoring a Java file; possible future use is not a reason to retain them.

In modules already depending on framework-core, prefer `NullSafe.copyToList`, `copyToSet`, or `copyToMap` according to the required immutable container type, without a redundant `Require.noNulls` check. These methods normalize a null container to an empty container and do not accept a custom exception supplier; use them only when the input contract and technical-exception semantics permit it.

In modules already depending on framework-core, prefer `Require.noNulls` when only collection or Map null-element checking is needed. It rejects null containers, allows empty containers, and checks both Map keys and values. Its exception-supplier overload uses the supplied exception for null containers, elements, keys, and values; business checks follow the business-exception rule.

retired.text: Prefer `NullSafe.forEach` for null-element checking alone; prefer `NullSafe.copyOf` when an immutable copy is also needed, without a redundant `forEach` check.
retired.reason: Split checking-only and immutable-copy selection into independent rules, update the API names, and define null-container contract boundaries separately.
